blocks.x: Industrial IoT & Sensor Fabric as delivered by Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, the platforms involved and the outcomes we commit to at each gate.

Brownfield plants cannot gut-and-replace; sensor network must retrofit. We engineer the sensing layer for real environments: environment-rated devices (IP-rated, Ex-certified where needed), retrofit mounting on existing assets, protocol translation from fieldbuses (Modbus, PROFINET, CAN) and raw sensors into OPC UA / MQTT Sparkplug B, and a governed telemetry pipeline with device registry, provisioning and OTA updates. Power and connectivity constraints get engineered answers: LoRaWAN/NB-IoT for wide-area, private 5G for dense mobile, edge gateways aggregating at the line.

The governance layer is what separates a sensor deployment from a sensor network: device lifecycle ownership, data contracts per signal, calibration schedules, and quality gates on ingestion. Clients get telemetry they can build twins, models and control loops on — because the timestamps are trustworthy, the units are consistent and the lineage is known.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
